newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Inverted FX volatility curves flatten.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Inverted FX volatility curves flatten.

text.p: The inverted volatility curves for most dollar-pair options flattened as spot dollar/mark met strong resistance near early highs and dollar/yen hovered in the lower 116-yen area, dealers said.

Even though the greenback briefly rose to a high of 1.7340 marks earlier in the day, its highest level in about a month, shorter dated options were sold fairly aggressively to lead the whole curve lower.
"It's counter-intuitive," said Ted Voorhees, a senior options dealer at Deutsche Bank in New York. "Maybe some guys are taking profit, maybe some exotics are going through."
He noted a general wariness to be long options and that dealers whose bids were getting hit quickly turned around to offset their positions, traders said.
"It's the domino effect," he said. "But if spot goes up another 20 points (0.2 pfennigs toward 1.7350 marks), they'll be paying the offers again."

One-month dollar/mark implied volatility lost about a quarter point on the day to 9.7/9.9 percent by U.S. midsession, while one-week fell more than half a point to about 8.8/9.4. One-year was off about 0.1 at 9.5/9.8 percent.
A U.S. bank dealer in New York said most of the selling seemed to be coming out of Europe.

Despite the softer volatilities today, traders said the market remained more sensitive to the dollar's upside as most people still expected the dollar to gain on the mark in the intermediate term, given lingering uncertainties over the fate of the single European currency.

Upside strike prices were still favored in risk reversals, the cost of swapping equally out-of-the-money puts and calls. One-month 25-delta was pegged at 0.2/0.5 point skewed for mark puts, little changed from Tuesday.
Dollar/yen options were also subdued, particularly the front end, reflecting spot's reluctance to move out of the 116.00-116.50 yen range.
"I think they actually represent a fairly good value, but honestly we haven't seen very much U.S. corporate hedging interest around," the U.S. bank trader said.

Still, the one-month maturity remained the curve's peak as it covers the June 20-22 Group of Seven summit, the Bank of Japan's "tankan" report due out on June 25 and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for July 1-2.
"Definitely there's interest in that one-month period," the U.S. bank trader said.

One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 10.1/10.4 percent, down about half a point from late Tuesday. Volatilities for three-month out to one-year were about 0.1 point lower at 9.9/10.1 percent.

One-week continued to gap lower, shedding about half a point on the day to 10.0/11.0 percent, as it became an obvious target for gamma-sellers amid prospects of continued range-trading in spot for the coming days.
